ideas.risks: It will not solve the fixed-constant beta edge unless the definition allows gamma to shrink with representation size. The span-capture lemma or LPN reduction may need tighter quantifiers than the solver sketch gives.
ideas.summary: Formalize the parity/LPN near-separation for gamma = Theta(1/n): prove the span-capture weak learner with exact constants, sample size, validation step, and then prove that a strong improper agnostic learner under uniform RCN would break LPN via Goldreich-Levin-style recovery from an arbitrary evaluable predictor.
ideas.title: Parity Near-Separation Audit
ideas.why_promising: This is the most concrete new object from iteration 8. Even if it only yields a parameterized warning note, it sharply clarifies the fixed-versus-shrinking slack boundary.

ideas.risks: Most products make the weak side as hard as noisy parity at constant noise. Constants, validation, or table-learning escapes may destroy the intended separation.
ideas.summary: Investigate whether the inverse-polynomial parity near-separation can be converted into a fixed-constant gamma separation by direct products, block mixtures, noise padding, or meta-classes. Require that the resulting class has a distribution-free OPT+beta weak learner for a fixed beta<1/2, while strong improper learning still implies LPN-like prediction hardness.
ideas.title: Amplify Parity Gap
ideas.why_promising: If possible, this would turn the solver's near miss into a genuine conditional counterexample. If impossible, the no-go would explain why fixed constant slack is qualitatively different.

ideas.risks: The constructed weak learner may be too artificial, white-box removable, or fail to arise under the actual DCHP query distributions. It may remain only a black-box obstruction.
ideas.summary: Test whether arbitrary Set-Cover-hard sparse-majority bags can be realized as bags generated by a semantically valid weak learner inside a DCHP-style procedure, perhaps using rare-slice junk or query-programmed outputs. The target is either a reduction showing generated bags can be worst-case, or a structural property showing why they cannot.
ideas.title: Generated-Bag Hardness
ideas.why_promising: Current sparse-majority ERM hardness is only for arbitrary bags. This direction attacks the main loophole in using that hardness against the DCHP positive route.

ideas.risks: The hidden clean margin may not transfer to noisy validation labels. Set-Cover hardness may persist under the relevant margin promises. Even a selector theorem would not solve hidden-clean tuple generation.
ideas.summary: Look for a margin-promised selector for the exact DCHP class sign(B^(T)): prove or refute that a clean hidden margin certificate can be converted into an efficiently optimizable nonnegative convex vote and rounded to a T-wise integer majority using only observable noisy data.
ideas.title: Margin Selector Route
ideas.why_promising: This isolates a concrete positive bottleneck not ruled out by worst-case proper ERM hardness, especially if DCHP-generated instances have extra margin or structure.

ideas.risks: Low-mass regions under one query can become high-mass after later adaptive filters. Arbitrary hypothesis handles may defeat compression. No global cover may exist for hidden-clean queries.
ideas.summary: Explore distribution-dependent canonicalization of weak learner outputs: replace global Range(A) control by query-wise equivalence classes, validation-based pruning, or covers under the realized query marginals. Determine whether this yields bounded effective dual VC or finite realized bags sufficient for DCHP-style analysis.
ideas.title: Quotient The Weak Range
ideas.why_promising: Rare-slice junk refutes global range control, but it may be irrelevant under the distributions actually queried. A quotient theorem would be a plausible positive escape.

ideas.risks: Distribution-free low-noise signed approximation is very strong. Many candidates expose labels publicly, are finite-domain table-learnable, or only have recovery/refutation hardness rather than arbitrary improper prediction hardness.
ideas.summary: Search beyond fixed-arity CSPs for succinct-domain hard-band candidates: planted synchronization, group-labeled constraints, algebraic code families, or low-rank constraint systems with efficient low-noise signed/weighted approximation below gamma but conjectured hard improper prediction under RCN noise eta>=gamma.
ideas.title: Hard-Band Candidate Search
ideas.why_promising: The approximation-gap template remains the cleanest negative route. Iteration 8 shows parity gives the hardness side but not constant low-noise weak learning; other algebraic families might split these two regimes.

ideas.risks: The model may become too restricted to inform the atlas edge. Charging returned handles and evaluation access precisely is technically delicate, and spike/heavy-atom queries need separate treatment.
ideas.summary: Build a stopped-process random-target oracle barrier: define allowed query grammar, route public-witness and empirical-spike low-OPT queries, charge oracle outputs and evaluation access to transcript information, and prove that no polynomial wrapper creates a low-posterior chunk or strong predictor before enough target information is leaked.
ideas.title: Stopped-Process Barrier
ideas.why_promising: It would turn many local posterior/filter obstructions into one precise theorem, giving critics a clean benchmark for any claimed black-box positive proof.

ideas.risks: The assumption may be too strong to hold for natural weak learners, and it does not follow from fixed-slack weak learning alone. Hidden clean discovery remains costly if the global clean mass is small.
ideas.summary: State and prove a conditional positive theorem under global final-classifier compression: a complete successful boosting trajectory or final classifier is encoded by O(log poly(s,1/epsilon)) clean examples plus enumerable advice, not by per-round clean witnesses. Then test whether known weak learners or DCHP transcripts satisfy this stronger compression property.
ideas.title: Global Compression Theorem
ideas.why_promising: This gives a precise positive benchmark that avoids the per-call logarithmic witness trap and could subsume the random clean-witness menu route.
